overall: At 5:49 AM ET, Washington DC is sitting at 77.0°F with a running max of 78.8°F — still firmly in overnight territory with the diurnal heating cycle yet to engage. Temperature has been flat (velocity +0.0°F/hr) under 100% cloud cover with a tropical airmass in place (dewpoint ~70°F), and an active Flood Watch citing a slow-moving frontal zone and excessive rainfall risk this afternoon and evening. Despite the muggy, stormy setup, temperatures are expected to surge well above current levels before afternoon convection potentially acts as a cap.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are tightly and bullishly clustered — GFS 93°F, HRRR 92.2°F, ECMWF 91°F — while NBM stands as a clear outlier at 85.8°F, likely baking in convective cooling from the 60% afternoon storm probability. The NWS text forecast aligns near the middle at ~90°F with a heat index of 103°F, and the D1_NOW model tops out at 90–91F (12.2%). The META model distribution is unusually spread and bimodal, flagging elevated uncertainty from convective interference with a surprising mode at 78–79F (24.4%), though this almost certainly reflects model uncertainty rather than a physical expectation given the current 78.8°F early-morning running max.
max_temp_prediction: Best estimate is a TMAX near 89–91°F, anchored by the NWS 90°F forecast and strong NWP consensus in the 91–93°F range, discounted modestly for the meaningful afternoon thunderstorm risk that could clip the peak before full heating is realized. The active even-bucket Kalshi market's top bucket is 90–91F at 12.2%, which is the most defensible single target given current evidence; however, the ensemble signals a Tier 4 / no-trade condition due to high distributional entropy and model spread, so conviction is low. Confidence is moderate at best — the tropical airmass supports a high heat index but the storm timing relative to the temperature peak is the key wildcard.
